author: Mark Atwood
text:
Filing 'human' because the bead presents three non-equivalent options for replacing HashMap in SetResponse + JmapRequest.created_ids + JmapResponse.created_ids, and the decision is workspace-architectural (changes the public type signature on canonical foundation types, ripples through 30 sibling crates per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates").

Option (a) serde_json::Map<String, T>: consistent with the extras pattern, lexicographic-key-order iteration under default serde_json features. Bead-concern (1) ties this to JMAP-6xs8.18 (the existing pub extra: serde_json::Map<...> shape is already a serde_json coupling forever-commitment; widening that coupling to SetResponse maps deepens the commitment). Note: bd:JMAP-6xs8.18 is itself filed as 'human' for the same workspace-architectural reason — deciding (a) here is a downstream consequence of deciding the .18 question first.

Option (b) BTreeMap<Id, T> / BTreeMap<String, T>: std-only, deterministic via natural ordering. Avoids the serde_json coupling but the K type differs per field (Id vs String for the creation-id half of SetResponse), creating typed inconsistency the current HashMap shape doesn't have (HashMap<Id, ...> and HashMap<String, ...> live in different fields on the same struct already — moving to BTreeMap preserves that).

Option (c) workspace newtype SetMap<K, V>: maximum encapsulation, future storage change is non-breaking. But adds a new type to the canonical foundation that every consumer learns; deviates from the rest of the workspace's idiom of using std/serde_json containers directly.

Recommendation: defer to the planned 0.2.0 coordinated bump (workspace root Cargo.toml lines 55-59) and tie the decision to .18 — if .18 ratifies the serde_json::Map coupling, then (a) is the consistent choice; if .18 rejects the coupling and moves to a newtype, then (c) becomes the natural choice; if .18 accepts the coupling but the maintainer prefers std-only here, (b) is viable. The three options collapse to one once .18 is decided.

Rationale for not autonomously picking:
- Workspace-architectural decision touching the canonical foundation.
- Wire-compatible with all three options, so no spec-conformance pressure to pick one over another.
- The decision interlocks with bd:JMAP-6xs8.18 (which is itself filed as human).

Awaiting maintainer direction on .18 first, then this becomes a mechanical follow-through.
